verifiable-quality-gates.why: every fix is pinned by a test that FAILS when reverted: install-hooks arms only at the repo root (#143), neither it nor esk-genesis clobbers pre-commit/.git-hooks (#131), and the pre-push fails closed on a corrupt/gates-less/zero-gates manifest (#122)
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added ISSUE-143/131/122 discrimination cases; the install-hooks tests now run the helper from <repo>/.githooks as it ships; full suite 720 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: changing when and where core.hooksPath is written (repo-root-only, no-clobber) and making the pre-push fail closed is architecturally significant and recorded in one ADR
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0077 covering the four fixes and the honest limits (best-effort arming, hasActiveGitHook erring toward not-clobbering)
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: each fix is pinned at the level that owns it: an integration test that spawns the real helper / hook / esk-genesis against a fixture git repo and asserts the real config state or exit code
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: fixture-based tests for the nested-repo, pre-commit-present, existing-hook, and corrupt/gates-less/zero-gates manifest paths
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the non-happy paths were enumerated and committed: run from a nested package, a pre-commit repo, a repo with an existing hook, and a push with a corrupt / gates-less / empty manifest
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: node:test cases, each asserting the real core.hooksPath value or the hook's exit code
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

skeptical-audit.why: ADR-0077 states the honest limits rather than overclaiming: arming is best-effort (the helper never fails the install) and hasActiveGitHook can over-decline, erring toward NOT clobbering; CI stays the enforcing authority
skeptical-audit.what: recorded each limit in ADR-0077 and verified the suite green before claiming it
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review was run on the hook-arming delta before the PR, checking the repo-root comparison, the no-clobber detection, and the pre-push fail-closed boundary
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in a fresh subagent and recorded it in the arch-review log
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no user input/auth/session/secret/upload surface; #143 is a confused-deputy containment fix (never write another repo's git config) handled as defensive correctness, not a product security control that needs an @security scenario

pattern-selector.why: no new feature, class, module or data flow; the fixes reuse the existing installer/hook structure

arch-encode.why: the fixes are enforced by discrimination tests, not a new rules-file entry

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no PII, retention, migration, backup or audit logic; this is installer/hook tooling

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system, service, database or integration architecture changed

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature-flag or rollback mechanism; this is a local pre-push pre-flight and its arming, not a release path

sre-operational-readiness.why: no SLI/SLO, alert, runbook or production-operability surface

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing or UI surface; developer-facing installer/hook tooling

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or frontend code; developer-facing installer/hook tooling

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing flow, screen, form or copy; developer-facing installer/hook tooling
